title: How to write a quote for a roofing job
summary: Paste your roofing job notes into ChatGPT and get a clear quote a homeowner can say yes to. Check the price, deposit, and what's included before you send it.

tests.prompt:
You help a roofer write a job quote a homeowner can understand. Draft only. Do not send it.

Fill in these details. If a line is blank, write UNKNOWN and do not guess.

Customer name: [CUSTOMER NAME]
Job address: [JOB ADDRESS]
Roof type and work: [WORK]
Squares or roof size: [SIZE]
Materials: [MATERIALS]
What's included: [INCLUDED]
What's not included: [NOT INCLUDED]
Price: [PRICE]
Deposit: [DEPOSIT]
Start and finish window: [TIMELINE]
How long the quote is good: [QUOTE EXPIRATION]
Your name and business: [YOUR NAME]
Your phone: [YOUR PHONE]
Email or text: [CHANNEL]

Rules:
- Never invent details; if something is missing, ask or mark it UNKNOWN.
- Do not add work, materials, warranties, or discounts that are not in the details.
- Do not change the price or the deposit. Copy them exactly.
- Do not promise a start date that is not in [TIMELINE].
- Keep the tone plain and friendly, like a note a homeowner can read once and understand.
- No slang, no pressure, no "limited time" language unless [QUOTE EXPIRATION] has a date.

Output format:
Return these headings only:
Channel
Subject (NONE if this is a text)
Quote (180 words or fewer for email, 90 words or fewer for a text)
What's included
What's not included
Price and deposit
Next step
Facts used
Unknown
The next step should ask them to reply or call [YOUR PHONE] if they want to book. Do not add a payment link unless one was provided.

setup.agent: Paste this into ChatGPT, or into the chat assistant you already use.
steps: On one note, write the customer's name, the job address, the work (for example a tear-off and new shingles), the roof size, materials, what is included, what is not, the price, the deposit, and the start and finish window.
Add your name, business name, phone, and whether you will send this as an email or a text. If you do not know a detail, leave it blank instead of guessing.
Open ChatGPT. Copy the ChatGPT prompt, paste it in, and replace every [BRACKET] with the details from your note. If a line is blank, type UNKNOWN in that bracket.
Read the quote beside your note. Confirm the address, the work, the price, the deposit, and the dates. Cross out any warranty, discount, or extra work you did not write down.
Copy the finished quote into your email or the customer's text thread. Send it yourself only after those numbers match.
setup.approvalStep: You check the address, the work, the price, and the deposit against your note, then you send the quote yourself. ChatGPT only writes the draft.
failureModes: The draft adds a warranty or a material you did not name. Delete that line before you send it.
The price or deposit is rounded or split in a way you did not write. Copy your numbers back in exactly.
Two jobs were pasted together and the quote mixes addresses or measurements. Run one address at a time.
The draft promises a start date you cannot keep. Keep only the window that is on your note.

faq.q: Do I have to use ChatGPT for this?
faq.a: No. Use the prompt for the assistant you already have, whether that is ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, or Muse. The important part is replacing the brackets with your real job details and checking the price before you send it.

faq.q: What if I do not know the roof size yet?
faq.a: Leave the size blank so the draft marks it UNKNOWN. Measure or confirm the squares yourself, then add that number before you send the quote. Do not let the draft guess the size.

faq.q: Can this send the quote for me?
faq.a: No. It only writes the draft. You paste it into email or a text, check the address and the numbers, and send it yourself.

job: Paste roofing job notes and get a clear quote a homeowner can understand and accept.
who: Roofers and small roofing companies who write their own quotes and want a plain email or text a homeowner can say yes to.

example.scenario: A small roofing company is quoting a tear-off and new architectural shingles on a one-story house.
example.input:
Customer name: Sam Rivera
Job address: 14 Pine Street
Roof type and work: Full tear-off, new underlayment, architectural shingles
Squares or roof size: 22 squares
Materials: Architectural shingles, ice-and-water on eaves
What's included: Tear-off, haul-away, underlayment, shingles, ridge vent, cleanup
What's not included: Plywood or fascia repairs, gutters
Price: $14,800
Deposit: $4,400 to book
Start and finish window: The week of April 13, two days on site if the weather holds
How long the quote is good: 30 days
Your name and business: Jordan at Ridge Line Roofing
Your phone: 555-0172
Email or text: email
example.output:
Channel: email
Subject: Roofing quote for 14 Pine Street

Quote:
Hi Sam, this is Jordan at Ridge Line Roofing. Thank you for walking the roof at 14 Pine Street with me. Here is the quote for a full tear-off and new architectural shingles on the 22-square roof.

What's included: Tear-off and haul-away, underlayment, ice-and-water on the eaves, architectural shingles, a ridge vent, and a full cleanup.

What's not included: Plywood or fascia repairs, and gutter work. If we find damaged boards, I will show you and price that separately before we go ahead.

Price and deposit: The job is $14,800. A $4,400 deposit books the week of April 13. We expect two days on site if the weather holds. This quote is good for 30 days.

Next step: Reply to this email or call me at 555-0172 if you would like to book.

Facts used: 14 Pine Street, 22 squares, $14,800, $4,400, week of April 13, 30 days.
Unknown: none.
example.notes: Made-up names and numbers, only to show the shape of a clear quote.
